claim: Burst firing of mouse inner hair cells prior to hearing onset requires P2RY1 autoreceptors expressed by inner supporting cells.
source: We show that burst firing of mouse inner hair cells prior to hearing onset requires P2RY1 autoreceptors expressed by inner supporting cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including pharmacological inhibition and genetic deletion experiments.

claim: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux from inner supporting cells.
source: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux and depolarization of hair cells, as well as osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells that dramatically increased the extracellular space and speed of K+ redistribution.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological recordings and imaging data shown in the figures.

claim: P2RY1 activation causes depolarization of hair cells.
source: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux and depolarization of hair cells, as well as osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells that dramatically increased the extracellular space and speed of K+ redistribution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through whole-cell recordings from inner hair cells showing inward currents upon P2RY1 activation.

claim: P2RY1 activation causes osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells.
source: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux and depolarization of hair cells, as well as osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells that dramatically increased the extracellular space and speed of K+ redistribution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through transmitted light imaging showing crenations (cell shrinkage) of inner supporting cells.

claim: Osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells dramatically increases the extracellular space.
source: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux and depolarization of hair cells, as well as osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells that dramatically increased the extracellular space and speed of K+ redistribution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments measuring K+ tail currents in hair cells that indicate changes in extracellular K+ concentration consistent with increased extracellular volume.

claim: Osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells increases the speed of K+ redistribution.
source: P2RY1 activation triggers K+ efflux and depolarization of hair cells, as well as osmotic shrinkage of supporting cells that dramatically increased the extracellular space and speed of K+ redistribution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experiments showing that K+ tail currents shift outward following P2RY1 stimulation, indicating enhanced K+ clearance.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY1 suppresses neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppressed neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release, but unexpectedly enhanced their tonic firing, as water resorption by supporting cells reduced the extracellular space, leading to K+ accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by juxtacellular recordings from spiral ganglion neurons showing reduced burst frequency with MRS2500 application.

claim: Genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppresses neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppressed neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release, but unexpectedly enhanced their tonic firing, as water resorption by supporting cells reduced the extracellular space, leading to K+ accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by recordings from P2ry1 knockout mice showing altered firing patterns.

claim: P2RY1 inhibition enhances tonic firing of neurons.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppressed neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release, but unexpectedly enhanced their tonic firing, as water resorption by supporting cells reduced the extracellular space, leading to K+ accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by recordings showing increased non-burst firing following P2RY1 inhibition.

claim: Water resorption by supporting cells following P2RY1 inhibition reduces the extracellular space.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppressed neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release, but unexpectedly enhanced their tonic firing, as water resorption by supporting cells reduced the extracellular space, leading to K+ accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and inferred from experiments showing progressive inward currents in hair cells following P2RY1 inhibition, consistent with K+ accumulation in a reduced extracellular volume.

claim: Reduction of extracellular space following P2RY1 inhibition leads to K+ accumulation.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or genetic disruption of P2RY1 suppressed neuronal burst firing by reducing K+ release, but unexpectedly enhanced their tonic firing, as water resorption by supporting cells reduced the extracellular space, leading to K+ accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experiments showing progressive inward currents in hair cells and supporting cells following P2RY1 inhibition.

claim: Purinergic signaling in supporting cells regulates hair cell excitability by controlling the volume of the extracellular space.
source: These studies indicate that purinergic signaling in supporting cells regulates hair cell excitability by controlling the volume of the extracellular space.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Neurons in developing sensory pathways exhibit spontaneous bursts of electrical activity.
source: Neurons in developing sensory pathways exhibit spontaneous bursts of electrical activity that are critical for survival, maturation and circuit refinement.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Spontaneous bursts of electrical activity in developing sensory pathways are critical for survival, maturation and circuit refinement.
source: Neurons in developing sensory pathways exhibit spontaneous bursts of electrical activity that are critical for survival, maturation and circuit refinement.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: In the auditory system, intrinsically generated activity arises within the cochlea.
source: In the auditory system, intrinsically generated activity arises within the cochlea, but the molecular mechanisms that initiate this activity remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by prior literature cited in the introduction.

claim: The molecular mechanisms that initiate spontaneous activity in the cochlea remain poorly understood.
source: In the auditory system, intrinsically generated activity arises within the cochlea, but the molecular mechanisms that initiate this activity remain poorly understood.
evidence: This statement establishes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Molecular guidance cues forge globally precise neuronal connections between distant brain areas.
source: While molecular guidance cues forge globally precise neuronal connections between distant brain areas (Dickson, 2002; Stoeckli, 2018), the organization of local connections is initially coarse and imprecise (Dhande et al., 2011; Kirkby et al., 2013; Sretavan and Shatz, 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The organization of local neuronal connections is initially coarse and imprecise.
source: While molecular guidance cues forge globally precise neuronal connections between distant brain areas (Dickson, 2002; Stoeckli, 2018), the organization of local connections is initially coarse and imprecise (Dhande et al., 2011; Kirkby et al., 2013; Sretavan and Shatz, 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intrinsically generated activity consists of periodic bursts of high frequency firing.
source: This intrinsically generated activity consists of periodic bursts of high frequency firing that promotes the survival and maturation of neurons in sensory pathways (Blankenship and Feller, 2010; Moody and Bosma, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Periodic bursts of high frequency firing promote the survival and maturation of neurons in sensory pathways.
source: This intrinsically generated activity consists of periodic bursts of high frequency firing that promotes the survival and maturation of neurons in sensory pathways (Blankenship and Feller, 2010; Moody and Bosma, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Disruption of precise patterning of electrical activity results in improper formation of topographic maps.
source: The precise patterning of this electrical activity appears crucial for refinement of local connections, as its disruption results in improper formation of topographic maps (Antón-Bolaños et al., 2019; Burbridge et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2011) and impaired maturation and specification of sensory neurons (Shrestha et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Disruption of precise patterning of electrical activity results in impaired maturation and specification of sensory neurons.
source: The precise patterning of this electrical activity appears crucial for refinement of local connections, as its disruption results in improper formation of topographic maps (Antón-Bolaños et al., 2019; Burbridge et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2011) and impaired maturation and specification of sensory neurons (Shrestha et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In all sensory systems examined, spontaneous burst firing arises within their respective developing sensory organs.
source: In all sensory systems that have been examined, spontaneous burst firing arises within their respective developing sensory organs (e.g. retina, olfactory neuroepithelium, and cochlea) (Blankenship and Feller, 2010; Yu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The mechanisms that induce spontaneous activity in the developing retina have been extensively explored.
source: Although the mechanisms that induce spontaneous activity in the developing retina have been extensively explored, much less is known about the key steps involved in triggering auditory neuron burst firing in the developing cochlea.
evidence: This statement establishes the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Much less is known about the key steps involved in triggering auditory neuron burst firing in the developing cochlea compared to the retina.
source: Although the mechanisms that induce spontaneous activity in the developing retina have been extensively explored, much less is known about the key steps involved in triggering auditory neuron burst firing in the developing cochlea.
evidence: This statement establishes the knowledge gap that motivates the study.

claim: The mechanisms responsible for initiating spontaneous activity are unique to each sensory system.
source: The mechanisms responsible for initiating spontaneous activity appear to be unique to each sensory system, reflecting adaptations to the structure and cellular composition of the sensory organs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a general principle in the field.

claim: One model proposes that burst firing initiation results from intermittent hyperpolarization of tonically active IHCs by cholinergic efferents.
source: One model proposes that the initiation of burst firing results from intermittent hyperpolarization of tonically active IHCs by cholinergic efferents (Johnson et al., 2011; Wang and Bergles, 2015), which provide prominent inhibitory input to IHCs prior to hearing onset (Glowatzki and Fuchs, 2000).
evidence: This describes one of two competing models in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Cholinergic efferents provide prominent inhibitory input to IHCs prior to hearing onset.
source: One model proposes that the initiation of burst firing results from intermittent hyperpolarization of tonically active IHCs by cholinergic efferents (Johnson et al., 2011; Wang and Bergles, 2015), which provide prominent inhibitory input to IHCs prior to hearing onset (Glowatzki and Fuchs, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Transient activation of acetylcholine receptors in acutely isolated cochleae causes IHCs to switch from sustained to burst firing.
source: While transient activation of acetylcholine receptors in acutely isolated cochleae caused IHCs to switch from sustained to burst firing (Johnson et al., 2011), in vivo recordings from auditory brainstem revealed that neuronal burst firing remains, with altered temporal structure, in α9 acetylcholine receptor knockout (KO) mice (Clause et al., 2014) that lack functional efferent signaling in IHCs (Clause et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Neuronal burst firing remains with altered temporal structure in α9 acetylcholine receptor knockout mice.
source: While transient activation of acetylcholine receptors in acutely isolated cochleae caused IHCs to switch from sustained to burst firing (Johnson et al., 2011), in vivo recordings from auditory brainstem revealed that neuronal burst firing remains, with altered temporal structure, in α9 acetylcholine receptor knockout (KO) mice (Clause et al., 2014) that lack functional efferent signaling in IHCs (Clause et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: α9 acetylcholine receptor knockout mice lack functional efferent signaling in IHCs.
source: While transient activation of acetylcholine receptors in acutely isolated cochleae caused IHCs to switch from sustained to burst firing (Johnson et al., 2011), in vivo recordings from auditory brainstem revealed that neuronal burst firing remains, with altered temporal structure, in α9 acetylcholine receptor knockout (KO) mice (Clause et al., 2014) that lack functional efferent signaling in IHCs (Clause et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Burst firing persists in IHCs and auditory neurons in cochleae maintained in vitro without functional efferents.
source: Burst firing also persists in IHCs and auditory neurons in cochleae maintained in vitro without functional efferents (Johnson et al., 2013; Tritsch et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cholinergic efferents modulate the temporal characteristics of bursts but are not essential to initiate each event.
source: These findings suggest that cholinergic efferents modulate the temporal characteristics of bursts, but are not essential to initiate each event.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cited findings presented in the introduction.

claim: IHCs are induced to fire bursts of action potentials by the release of K+ from nearby inner supporting cells.
source: An alternative model proposes that IHCs are induced to fire bursts of action potentials by the release of K+ from nearby inner supporting cells (ISCs), which together form a transient structure known as Köllikers organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge) that is prominent in the cochlea prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This describes the alternative model that the study supports.

claim: Inner supporting cells and inner hair cells together form a transient structure known as Kölliker's organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge).
source: An alternative model proposes that IHCs are induced to fire bursts of action potentials by the release of K+ from nearby inner supporting cells (ISCs), which together form a transient structure known as Köllikers organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge) that is prominent in the cochlea prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents anatomical knowledge.

claim: Kölliker's organ is prominent in the cochlea prior to hearing onset.
source: An alternative model proposes that IHCs are induced to fire bursts of action potentials by the release of K+ from nearby inner supporting cells (ISCs), which together form a transient structure known as Köllikers organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge) that is prominent in the cochlea prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents anatomical knowledge.

claim: K+ release from ISCs occurs following a cascade of events that begins with the spontaneous release of ATP and activation of purinergic autoreceptors.
source: K+ release from ISCs occurs following a cascade of events that begins with the spontaneous release of ATP and activation of purinergic autoreceptors (Tritsch et al., 2010a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Purinergic receptor activation induces an increase in intracellular Ca2+ in ISCs.
source: Purinergic receptor activation induces an increase in intracellular Ca2+ in ISCs, opening of Ca2+-activated Cl– channels (TMEM16A), efflux of Cl– and subsequently K+ to balance charge (Tritsch et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Purinergic receptor activation leads to opening of Ca2+-activated Cl– channels (TMEM16A) in ISCs.
source: Purinergic receptor activation induces an increase in intracellular Ca2+ in ISCs, opening of Ca2+-activated Cl– channels (TMEM16A), efflux of Cl– and subsequently K+ to balance charge (Tritsch et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Opening of TMEM16A channels leads to efflux of Cl– and subsequently K+ to balance charge.
source: Purinergic receptor activation induces an increase in intracellular Ca2+ in ISCs, opening of Ca2+-activated Cl– channels (TMEM16A), efflux of Cl– and subsequently K+ to balance charge (Tritsch et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The loss of ions during each event draws water out of ISCs through osmosis, leading to pronounced shrinkage (crenation) of ISCs.
source: The loss of ions during each event draws water out of ISCs through osmosis, leading to pronounced shrinkage (crenation) of ISCs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a known consequence of ion efflux.

claim: The molecular identity of the purinergic receptors involved in spontaneous activity has remained elusive.
source: While these pathways have been extensively studied in vitro, the molecular identity of the purinergic receptors has remained elusive and few manipulations of this pathway have been performed in vivo, limiting our understanding of how spontaneous activity in the cochlea influences patterns of neuronal activity in auditory centers at this critical stage of development.
evidence: This statement establishes a key knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Few manipulations of the purinergic signaling pathway have been performed in vivo.
source: While these pathways have been extensively studied in vitro, the molecular identity of the purinergic receptors has remained elusive and few manipulations of this pathway have been performed in vivo, limiting our understanding of how spontaneous activity in the cochlea influences patterns of neuronal activity in auditory centers at this critical stage of development.
evidence: This statement establishes a methodological gap that the study addresses.

claim: The key initial step in generation of spontaneous activity in the auditory system involves activation of P2RY1 autoreceptors in ISCs.
source: Here, we show that the key initial step in generation of spontaneous activity in the auditory system involves activation of P2RY1 autoreceptors in ISCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: P2RY1 metabotropic receptors induce Ca2+ release from intracellular stores that allow TMEM16A channels to open.
source: These metabotropic receptors induce Ca2+ release from intracellular stores that allow TMEM16A channels to open.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experiments with thapsigargin and U73122.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY1 dramatically reduced burst firing in spiral ganglion neurons.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY1 or genetic deletion of P2ry1 dramatically reduced burst firing in spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) and blocked the coordinated, spatially restricted activation of ISCs, IHCs, and SGNs in the cochlea.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by juxtacellular recordings from SGNs.

claim: Genetic deletion of P2ry1 dramatically reduced burst firing in spiral ganglion neurons.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY1 or genetic deletion of P2ry1 dramatically reduced burst firing in spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) and blocked the coordinated, spatially restricted activation of ISCs, IHCs, and SGNs in the cochlea.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by recordings from P2ry1 KO mice.

claim: P2RY1 inhibition or deletion blocked the coordinated, spatially restricted activation of ISCs, IHCs, and SGNs in the cochlea.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY1 or genetic deletion of P2ry1 dramatically reduced burst firing in spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) and blocked the coordinated, spatially restricted activation of ISCs, IHCs, and SGNs in the cochlea.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by calcium imaging experiments.

claim: P2RY1 activation promotes the dissipation of K+ away from IHCs by increasing the volume of extracellular space.
source: Unexpectedly, P2RY1 activation also promoted the dissipation of K+ away from IHCs by increasing the volume of extracellular space.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by experiments measuring K+ tail currents.

claim: Inhibition of P2RY1 reduced the extracellular space and restricted the redistribution of K+ within the cochlear epithelium.
source: Conversely, inhibition of P2RY1 reduced the extracellular space and restricted the redistribution of K+ within the cochlear epithelium, causing IHCs to depolarize and fire tonically, demonstrating an important role for purinergic receptor-mediated extracellular space changes in controlling IHC excitability.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by experiments showing progressive inward currents following P2RY1 inhibition.

claim: Inhibition of P2RY1 causes IHCs to depolarize and fire tonically.
source: Conversely, inhibition of P2RY1 reduced the extracellular space and restricted the redistribution of K+ within the cochlear epithelium, causing IHCs to depolarize and fire tonically, demonstrating an important role for purinergic receptor-mediated extracellular space changes in controlling IHC excitability.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by recordings showing increased tonic firing.

claim: Acute inhibition of P2Y1 dramatically reduced burst firing of auditory neurons in isofrequency domains in vivo.
source: Using in vivo widefield epifluorescence imaging of the auditory midbrain in unanesthetized mice, we show that acute inhibition of P2Y1 dramatically reduced burst firing of auditory neurons in isofrequency domains.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by in vivo calcium imaging of the inferior colliculus.

claim: P2RY1 autoreceptors in non-sensory supporting cells in the cochlea play a crucial role in generating bursts of activity among neurons that will ultimately process similar frequencies of sound.
source: Together, these data indicate P2RY1 autoreceptors in non-sensory supporting cells in the cochlea play a crucial role in generating bursts of activity among neurons that will ultimately process similar frequencies of sound, providing the means to initiate the maturation of auditory pathways before hearing onset.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the introduction, synthesizing the findings.

claim: Spontaneous inward currents and crenations in ISCs were abolished following incubation with BAPTA-AM (100 μM).
source: Spontaneous inward currents and crenations were abolished following a 15 min incubation of excised cochlea in BAPTA-AM (100 μM), a cell permeant Ca2+ chelator (Figure 1B–F), and after depleting intracellular Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin (2 μM), an inhibitor of endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (Figure 1B–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Spontaneous inward currents and crenations in ISCs were abolished after depleting intracellular Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin (2 μM).
source: Spontaneous inward currents and crenations were abolished following a 15 min incubation of excised cochlea in BAPTA-AM (100 μM), a cell permeant Ca2+ chelator (Figure 1B–F), and after depleting intracellular Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin (2 μM), an inhibitor of endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (Figure 1B–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Ca2+ release from intracellular stores is necessary for spontaneous electrical activity in ISCs.
source: These data suggest that Ca2+ release from intracellular stores is necessary for spontaneous electrical activity in ISCs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results with BAPTA-AM and thapsigargin.

claim: Neither spontaneous currents nor crenations in ISCs were affected by ryanodine (10 μM).
source: However, neither spontaneous currents nor crenations were affected by ryanodine (10 μM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Engagement of a Gq-coupled purinergic autoreceptor is a critical first step in initiating PLC-mediated Ca2+ release from intracellular stores and subsequent activation of TMEM16A channels.
source: Together, these results suggest that engagement of a Gq-coupled purinergic autoreceptor is a critical first step in initiating PLC-mediated Ca2+ release from intracellular stores and subsequent activation of TMEM16A channels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results with various inhibitors.

claim: Non-sensory cells in the developing mouse cochlea express P2RY1 mRNA at high levels, >100 fold higher than any other P2RY.
source: Gene expression studies in the developing mouse cochlea revealed that non-sensory cells express P2RY1 mRNA at high levels, >100 fold higher than any other P2RY (Figure 2A; Scheffer et al., 2015) and that expression of this receptor progressively increases during early postnatal development (Figure 2A, inset) concurrent with increases in spontaneous activity (Tritsch and Bergles, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, shown in Figure 2A, and supported by a citation.

claim: P2RY1 expression progressively increases during early postnatal development concurrent with increases in spontaneous activity.
source: Gene expression studies in the developing mouse cochlea revealed that non-sensory cells express P2RY1 mRNA at high levels, >100 fold higher than any other P2RY (Figure 2A; Scheffer et al., 2015) and that expression of this receptor progressively increases during early postnatal development (Figure 2A, inset) concurrent with increases in spontaneous activity (Tritsch and Bergles, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, shown in Figure 2A inset, and supported by citations.

claim: P2RY1 is expressed within ISCs but not IHCs.
source: To determine which cells in the sensory epithelium express P2RY1, we isolated cochleae from P2ry1-LacZ reporter mice and performed X-gal staining. Intense blue labeling was present along the entire length of the cochlea within Kölliker's organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge; Figure 2B), and cross-sections of cochlea revealed that staining was present within ISCs, but not IHCs (Myosin VIIA, Figure 2C), indicating that P2RY1 is appropriately localized to sense ATP release from ISCs prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: P2RY1 is appropriately localized to sense ATP release from ISCs prior to hearing onset.
source: To determine which cells in the sensory epithelium express P2RY1, we isolated cochleae from P2ry1-LacZ reporter mice and performed X-gal staining. Intense blue labeling was present along the entire length of the cochlea within Kölliker's organ (Greater Epithelial Ridge; Figure 2B), and cross-sections of cochlea revealed that staining was present within ISCs, but not IHCs (Myosin VIIA, Figure 2C), indicating that P2RY1 is appropriately localized to sense ATP release from ISCs prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the localization data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Acute inhibition of P2RY1 with MRS2500 (1 µM) markedly reduced both spontaneous ISC currents and crenations.
source: Acute inhibition of P2RY1 with MRS2500 (1 µM) markedly reduced both spontaneous ISC currents (Figure 3B,C) and crenations (Figure 3D,E); near complete inhibition occurred within minutes at both room temperature (Figure 3B,C) and near physiological temperature (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–G), with only sporadic, small amplitude events remaining that were not mediated by purinergic receptors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Near complete inhibition of spontaneous ISC activity by MRS2500 occurred within minutes at both room temperature and near physiological temperature.
source: Acute inhibition of P2RY1 with MRS2500 (1 µM) markedly reduced both spontaneous ISC currents (Figure 3B,C) and crenations (Figure 3D,E); near complete inhibition occurred within minutes at both room temperature (Figure 3B,C) and near physiological temperature (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–G), with only sporadic, small amplitude events remaining that were not mediated by purinergic receptors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The amplitude and total charge transfer of ISC events were smaller in cochleae in P2ry1 KO mice relative to controls.
source: Consistent with the involvement of P2RY1, the amplitude and total charge transfer of ISC events (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B) and size of spontaneous crenations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D) were smaller in cochleae in P2ry1 KO mice relative to controls.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The size of spontaneous crenations was smaller in cochleae in P2ry1 KO mice relative to controls.
source: Consistent with the involvement of P2RY1, the amplitude and total charge transfer of ISC events (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B) and size of spontaneous crenations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D) were smaller in cochleae in P2ry1 KO mice relative to controls.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Supporting cells in P2ry1 KO mice exhibited more frequent, small amplitude currents that were not blocked by MRS2500 or broad-spectrum P2 receptor antagonists.
source: However, supporting cells in P2ry1 KO mice exhibited some aberrant, gain-of-function activity consisting of more frequent, small amplitude currents (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B), that were not blocked by MRS2500 or broad-spectrum P2 receptor antagonists (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Application of MRS2500 (1 µM) abolished spontaneous currents in IHCs.
source: To assess whether P2RY1 signaling is also required for periodic excitation of IHCs prior to hearing onset, we assessed the sensitivity of spontaneous IHC inward currents to MRS2500 (Figure 3F). Consistent with the supporting cell origin of IHC activity, application of MRS2500 (1 µM) also abolished spontaneous currents in IHCs (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: P2RY1 is the primary purinergic autoreceptor on ISCs responsible for inducing periodic excitation of IHCs prior to hearing onset.
source: Together, these data suggest that P2RY1 is the primary purinergic autoreceptor on ISCs responsible for inducing periodic excitation of IHCs prior to hearing onset.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results with MRS2500.

claim: A progressively increasing inward current appeared in both ISCs and IHCs with prolonged application of MRS2500.
source: Although P2RY1 inhibition abolished most transient inward currents in both ISCs and IHCs, a progressively increasing inward current (downward shift in baseline) appeared in both cell types with prolonged application of MRS2500 (Figure 3B,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B,F.

claim: The progressively increasing inward current in IHCs and ISCs following P2RY1 inhibition arises from accumulation of K+ released from cells in the organ of Corti.
source: Prior studies in CNS brain slices indicated that Gq-coupled purinergic receptors in astrocytes regulate extracellular K+ concentration and neuronal excitability (Wang et al., 2012). The slowly progressing nature of the response in IHCs and ISCs suggest that it may arise from accumulation of K+ released from cells in the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by experiments inhibiting K+ sources.

claim: When IHC and SGN excitation was inhibited with cadmium and tetrodotoxin, and K+ transporters were inhibited with ouabain and bumetanide, no inward current was induced in ISCs upon blocking P2RY1.
source: Indeed, when IHC and SGN excitation was inhibited with cadmium (CdCl2, 100 µM) and tetrodotoxin (TTX, 1 µM), and K+ transporters Na,K-ATPase and NKCC were inhibited with ouabain (10 µM) and bumetanide (50 µM), no inward current was induced in ISCs upon blocking P2RY1 (Figure 3H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3H,I.

claim: When whole cell recordings were performed from IHCs using an internal solution containing Cs+ and TEA, MRS2500 did not induce an inward current.
source: Similarly, if K+ accumulation is responsible for the current in IHCs, it should be abolished when the ability of IHCs to detect changes in K+ is reduced. When whole cell recordings were performed from IHCs using an internal solution containing Cs+ and TEA, which blocks most IHC K+ channels (Kros et al., 1998; Marcotti et al., 2003), MRS2500 also did not induce an inward current (Figure 3J,K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3J,K.

claim: P2RY1 has two distinct effects in the cochlea: it induces the transient inward currents that trigger IHC burst firing and it accelerates clearance of K+ away from IHCs within the organ of Corti.
source: Together, these results suggest that P2RY1 has two distinct effects in the cochlea; it induces the transient inward currents that trigger IHC burst firing (Figure 3F; see also Figure 6D,G) and it accelerates clearance of K+ away from IHCs within the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Focal P2RY1 stimulation with MRS2365 (10 μM) elicits an inward current and crenations in ISCs in control but not P2ry1 KO mice.
source: Focal P2RY1 stimulation with a selective agonist (MRS2365, 10 μM), which mimics the effect of endogenous ATP by eliciting an inward current and crenations in ISCs in control but not P2ry1 KO mice (Figure 4A–C), was combined with assessments of the reversal potential of K+ currents in IHCs using a voltage protocol similar to that used to assess extracellular K+ buildup at vestibular calyceal synapses (Lim et al., 2011) (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: Following transient stimulation of P2RY1, K+ tail currents in IHCs immediately shifted inward, consistent with an increase in extracellular K+.
source: Following transient stimulation of P2RY1, these K+ tail currents immediately shifted inward, as would be expected if extracellular K+ increases (Figure 4G,J), consistent with the effects metabotropic purinergic receptor stimulation on synaptically-evoked K+ currents in IHCs (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4G,J.

claim: After a few seconds following P2RY1 stimulation, K+ tail currents in IHCs shifted outward relative to baseline, indicative of a gradual decrease in extracellular K+ below that present prior to P2RY1 stimulation.

claim: Astrocytes are efficient K+ sinks due to their highly negative resting potential (~–85 mV) and large resting K+ conductance dominated by inward rectifying K+ channels and two-pore leak K+ channels.
source: Astrocytes are efficient K+ sinks due to their highly negative resting potential (~–85 mV) and large resting K+ conductance dominated by inward rectifying K+ channels (Olsen, 2012) and two-pore leak K+ channels (Ryoo and Park, 2016).

claim: K+ buffering in astrocytes is actively regulated by purinergic receptors.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents recent findings in the field.
